A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same IsSameObject study, with matching authors, research questions, and substantial shared experiments. The main text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices are readable and support comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original ADE20K probing results, constructed-image experiments, positional decoding, attention correlations, and segmentation/DINO-loss ablations.

after.justification: v2 retains original probing and ablation results and additionally reports baseline comparisons and complex-scene predictions.

M1.justification: The reported central probe changes from x^T W^T W y, a positive-semidefinite quadratic form, to a symmetric form with sign-flipped query/key projections. Appendix A.2.1 supplies full-rank and factorized symmetric implementations. This expands the admissible quadratic forms and revises the binding-space construction, beyond merely explaining the original formula.

E1.justification: ADE20K binding and segmentation tasks and the constructed car/boat scenarios remain. v2 Figures 2 and 9 add qualitative testing on complex natural scenes, including overlapping deer and retrieval of disconnected regions of one instance. This adds a limited occlusion scenario without adding a benchmark dataset.

E2.justification: v2 Appendix A.3.1/Figure 8 adds evaluated embedding-distance, cosine-similarity, dot-product, and self-attention baselines. The pairwise softmax object-class comparator in v1 Figure 2 is removed from the corresponding comparison. The pointwise instance comparator also loses its object/no-object classification loss. The evaluated backbone families remain unchanged.

E3.justification: Table 2 changes the reported segmentation metrics from accuracy to mIoU while retaining the numbers. The instance-query budget changes from 100 to 10, and batch size from 256 to 256 or 128. The appendix replaces its native-resolution CLIP comparison with an aligned-crop comparison and a common majority baseline, although patch alignment was already claimed in v1's main text. These are substantive reported setting changes; the PDFs do not establish which experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: v1 Appendix A.3's non-adjacent-layer binding experiment is removed, including the layer-15/layer-18 comparison. v2 adds complex-scene case studies testing instance separation and disconnected-region retrieval. The main shuffling/injection ablations, identical-object analyses, positional decoding, and attention correlations remain.

E5.justification: Both versions report Pearson correlations of 0.163 and 0.201 with permutation-test p < 0.001. Neither adds repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or a new uncertainty-estimation practice. v2's checklist reiterates the existing significance reporting.

E6.justification: Table 1 changes assigned accuracies: supervised ViT 76.3% to 84.2%, CLIP 84.2% to 82.9%, and MAE 82.9% to 76.3%; their associated improvement and peak-layer entries also change, while DINO entries remain. v2 adds baseline results, including the 77.16% distance baseline, and new layerwise and qualitative findings. The 83.3% cross-layer result is removed. These are revised reported results, without evidence establishing same-setting performance gains.

T1.justification: The quadratic and binding-space definitions change to signed query/key projections, with explicit symmetry and factorization constructions. The feature-plus-binding decomposition assumption remains. Appendix A.4.1's positional-symmetry argument and proof are retained; presenting the existing statement as Proposition A.1 does not constitute a new theoretical result.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction reverse an important conclusion about pretraining: v1 reports reliable binding in DINO, CLIP, and MAE but weak binding in supervised ViTs; v2 reports reliable binding in DINO, CLIP, and supervised ViTs but weak binding in MAE. The broader emergence, low-dimensional representation, and functional-role claims remain.

C2.justification: Section 3.3 changes supervised training from an explanation for weak binding to a source of useful identity supervision, and removes the explanation that MAE reconstruction promotes binding. v2 also removes the cross-layer retrieval hypothesis and the explicit attribution of positional-information removal to DINO's invariance objective. The limitations newly identify the mechanism linking different pretraining objectives to binding as unresolved; the existing causality caveat remains.

D1.justification: v2 adds Algorithms 1–2, normalization and regularization details, SVD-based projection recovery, exact pretrained checkpoint identifiers in Table 3, and explicit CLIP resizing/cropping instructions. It also specifies per-epoch patch sampling. These substantially expand reproducibility information beyond v1's setup description. The code link, GPU, optimizer, and training duration are retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds Adeli et al.'s affinity-based object-grouping work and positions the study as building on it; DINOv3 is added as the source of a demonstration image. MOVE, patch re-identification, and SAM 2 references are removed. The broader cognitive-science and object-centric-learning positioning remains.

P1.justification: The main section sequence remains, with localized rewrites of the introduction, probe descriptions, interpretations, limitations, and conclusion. Transformer-update equations move into the reorganized appendix, which separates probe details, baselines, and cross-model comparisons. A NeurIPS checklist is appended.

P2.justification: v2 substantially revises the visual presentation: it adds complex-scene and baseline figures, redraws the binding geometry and annotates the PCA schematic, adds heatmap color scales, and reorganizes backbone plots into cross-objective and normalized-depth comparisons. It also adds a checkpoint table and algorithm displays. Many existing distribution and attention plots are retained with resizing or relocation.

improvement.justification: The added controls, explicit algorithms, and checkpoint information improve assessability and reproducibility. However, the central cross-model conclusion reverses through reassignment of Table 1's score triplets, while Table 2 retains its numbers under different metric labels despite revised probe settings. The PDFs do not explain how these changes relate to corrections or rerun experiments. Consequently, the documentation gains are clear, but the net effect on scientific reliability and overall quality remains uncertain.
